gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-medefaidrin: Distinctive from the first glance, Gugi draws its letters with a marker-nib line that ignores direction, its open terminals letting the counters spill outward. And Noto Sans Medefaidrin, sans-serif and contemporary, does the quieter job, its high-rising lowercase keeping every curve free of ink pooling.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-meetei-mayek: Noto Sans Meetei Mayek brings large lowercase eyes and rounds that gap like a cracked bangle, a modern sans-serif with room to breathe. But Gugi is the memorable half, its strokes free of thin and thick, with open terminals that let the counters flow outward.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-mono: Sturdy, widely spaced words come from Noto Sans Mono, a sans-serif whose letters never bump and whose curves open generously. Noto Sans Mono is the steady half, though the pairing's boldest moment is Gugi, with crossbars as fat as the stems they join.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-mro: Chunky, confident, and a little toylike: Gugi draws with a pen-like line of constant weight and open-cut terminals. And Noto Sans Mro, a sans-serif, packs its words dense in the middle, with large entrances into each letter's inner space.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-multani: Noto Sans Multani gives the pair a lofty x-height and an e with a wide gap at its terminal, modern and sans in manner. Gugi, cut like laser-sheet at a single stroke width, does its best work in big, short lines.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Noto Sans Nabataean reads with lowercase standing almost cap-high and wide-open s curves, a plain sans with a contemporary feel. But Gugi is the one with attitude, its strokes of constant width like bent pipe, while the body simply carries the text.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-nag-mundari: Gugi stamps its headings with a t whose crossbar and stem share one width, and its open-cut terminals let the counters flow outward. And Noto Sans Nag Mundari, a sans with lowercase rivaling the capitals, makes the pair's strongest quality its sheer sturdiness.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Noto Sans Ogham is clean and contemporary, a plain sans with wide gaps in the e. Its bold-looking lowercase comes from the bodies being so high, and Gugi, with a thickness that never shifts with direction, matches that sturdiness.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-old-hungarian: Technical-pen steadiness meets friendly openness. Gugi is best at stating things loudly, its terminals cut open, while Noto Sans Old Hungarian, a plain sans, is best at staying legible, with large counters in a, e and s that hold open at tiny sizes.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-old-north-arabi: Neon tubing bent into letters: that is Gugi, constant in thickness and open at the terminals. Noto Sans Old North Arabian is the opposite in job, a sans that packs a dense lowercase band, its terminals pointing outward like a pair of tongs.
